title: Wall and car-contact response, squeeze, blocked reset and correction saturation
description: Contact fixture from BENCHMARKS.md 'Handling fixtures' (Contact row): maximum-speed frontal and oblique walls, head-on/rear-end/side pairs, a four-car squeeze, a blocked reset and correction-limit saturation. Maximum-speed entries are declared null: the documented 205-235 km/h stock range is a target, not a measurement, so no entry speed is pretended here. Barrier positions/angles, pair offsets and the 500 m section are authored initial values. The initial contact solver limits (0.25 m single / 0.5 m total correction) come from TECHNICAL_DESIGN and are carried as documented targets.

geometry.start_reference: World origin at the start of segment 0 on the centerline; forward -Z, right +X, up +Y.

segments.note: Authored 500 m asphalt section and width for the contact runs.

barriers.note: Head-on wall across the road at the authored impact zone; face perpendicular to the centerline tangent. The 12 m span is an authored initial value covering the authored 12 m road width so the wall_contact expectation is reconstructable; the height is undetermined until M2 course barrier content.

Authored oblique wall at the right road edge; 45 degrees and the 12 m span are authored initial values, not measured ones, so the oblique wall_contact expectation is reconstructable; the height is undetermined until M2 course barrier content.

driver.note: Full throttle held to the wall.
Full throttle held; the authored wall angle produces the oblique impact.

runs.description: Head-on car pair at maximum speed.

other_participants.note: Rival approaches from ahead on the same line; 120 m separation is an authored initial value.

runs.description: Rear-end pair: follower at maximum speed reaches a slower leader.

other_participants.note: 25 m initial gap is an authored initial value; the leader's speed is undetermined until M1.

runs.description: Side-contact pair: cars alongside at roughly one car width of separation.

other_participants.note: 1.9 m lateral separation is an authored initial value inside the 1.7-2.2 m car width envelope.

runs.description: Four-car squeeze: ego plus three rivals converging on one line.

driver.note: Converging positions are authored initial values; the resolver must prevent riding on top of one another or launching.

runs.description: Reset with the safe route anchor occupied; the car must search farther backward or be held harmlessly until clear, never moved forward.

driver.note: Reset requested after an authored 3 s hold, satisfying the GAME_DESIGN one-second reset hold. Anchor occupancy itself is course data (M2); this fixture declares the expected behavior.

runs.description: Deep overlap that saturates the documented correction limits; the resolver must remove inward relative velocity, log saturation and recover safely instead of tunneling.

other_participants.note: 0.6 m lateral offset is an authored deep-overlap starting condition, not a measured one.

timing_gates.purpose: Authored impact zone where the walls sit.

expected_events.note: Saturation must be logged and recovered safely, per TECHNICAL_DESIGN.

The run declares the expected response when the safe-route anchor is occupied: a backward search or a harmless hold. The occupancy itself is course-level (M2) data that this fixture does not construct, so the precondition is documented as unknown here rather than asserted as built.

comparison.purpose: Verify bounded contact response across the three starters at stock and maximum upgrades: no tunneling, launching, riding on top of another car, or unbounded impulse.

metrics.description: Record contact severity and post-contact velocity per run for later cosmetic-damage thresholds; GAME_DESIGN cosmetic thresholds (2 m/s loosen, 5 m/s single / 8 m/s accumulated detach) are M5 validation items, not asserted here.
